question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\text{E}[\frac{1}{{X}^{2}}].$

| $x$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
question.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\sum }_{x\in S}r(x)f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\frac{1}{{X}^{2}}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,f(x) \\  & =\frac{1}{{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2}}\cdot 0.3+\frac{1}{{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}\cdot 0.2+\frac{1}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}\cdot 0.5 \\  & =16\cdot 0.3+9\cdot 0.2+4\cdot 0.5 \\  & =4.8+1.8+2 \\  & =8.6.\end{aligned}
$$
